notes: Criterion 7: "'Well?' asked her mother. 'Well, Mother?' said the older girl." In a story about fetching water, an A1 learner may read 'Well' as a water well. It is faithful to Perrault and the scene still works, so not a blocker. Optional fix: "'So?' asked her mother. 'So, Mother?' said the older girl."
Criterion 7: "The mother ran at the younger girl." 'ran at' (to attack) may be read as 'ran to'. Optional fix: "The mother was very angry with the younger girl."

"Each word brings a flower or a diamond." The gift is only fully clear once the flowers fall from her mouth. Optional fix: "When you speak, a flower or a diamond comes out of your mouth." This would also match the A2 wording.
Quiz Q1: 'first' is not needed because only the poor woman came to her at the fountain. 'Who came to the younger girl at the fountain?' is cleaner.
"So I give you a present." is a little stilted. Optional: "So here is a present for you."
"She carried a big pitcher to a far fountain and back." 'a far fountain' is slightly unnatural. Optional: "She carried a big pitcher to a fountain far away and back."
"made herself so hated" is a participle construction close to the passive. It reads naturally, but a stricter B1 option is "made everyone hate her so much that even her own mother drove her away."

'weeping' appears twice in one sentence span ("sitting alone and weeping ... why she was weeping so bitterly"), and 'tumbling from her lips' echoes 'fall from her lips' just before it. Light variation would help, for example 'in tears' for the first 'weeping'.

summary: This is a faithful retelling of Perrault's 'Les Fées' at all five levels. The two encounters at the fountain, the half league walk, the silver flask, the 'Well?' exchange, the prince valuing the gift above a dowry and the elder sister's expulsion all match the original, and her death is softened to 'went far away', which suits a 4+ app. Grammar fits each level, all quizzes are keyed correctly, and only minor phrasing notes remain.
